stories.title: OpenAI employee arrested by FBI after listening device found at its office
stories.simple_summary: An employee at OpenAI was arrested because someone found a hidden listening device at the company's office. The device was apparently being used to secretly record conversations.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect ordinary people or small businesses. It's a legal matter involving one company's security.

stories.title: Kroger to lay off 3,000 corporate employees over 3 years as it leans into artificial intelligence
stories.simple_summary: Kroger, a large grocery store chain, is laying off 3,000 office workers over the next three years. The company says it is using AI to handle some of the work those people used to do.
stories.why_it_matters: If you shop at Kroger, prices and service might change as the company restructures. Small grocery stores should watch how big chains use AI to improve their operations.

stories.title: OpenAI engineer charged after listening device found in meeting room
stories.simple_summary: An engineer at OpenAI was charged by police after a hidden recording device was discovered in a meeting room at the company. The device was apparently placed there to spy on conversations.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a legal matter between individuals and law enforcement. It doesn't affect your daily life or business.

stories.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
stories.simple_summary: A company called Science Corporation put a tiny computer chip in a patient's eye to help restore their sight. The chip is meant for people with a specific eye disease that causes blindness.
stories.why_it_matters: This might matter to you if you or someone you know has this eye disease. It shows that AI and computer chips are starting to help with serious medical problems.

stories.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
stories.simple_summary: An AI company's leader predicts that in the future, people will have personal AI assistants at home as normal as refrigerators or televisions. These assistants would run partly on your device and partly on company computers in the cloud.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a prediction about what might happen someday, not something happening now. Most older people and small business owners don't need to worry about this yet.

stories.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
stories.simple_summary: A company called Industrial Next is building robots that can learn new factory jobs very quickly, switching between different tasks in minutes instead of taking weeks to retrain. This is meant for jobs that are tricky and require careful work.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a factory or manufacturing business, robots that can switch tasks faster could save you money and time. Most other small business owners won't be directly affected.

stories.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
stories.simple_summary: A CEO from an AI company says that AI leaders should stop warning the public about AI dangers. He believes the focus on risks is preventing people from seeing AI's good uses.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech leaders debating AI policy. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Saudi man charged with planting 'sophisticated' recording device in OpenAI office
stories.simple_summary: A Saudi man was charged with placing a hidden surveillance device inside an OpenAI office. The device was described as sophisticated, meaning it was well made and hard to detect.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a criminal case involving one company. It doesn't affect most people or small business owners.

stories.title: AI in your oven? Anthropic warns models ‘months away’ from self-replication on smart devices
stories.simple_summary: A company called Anthropic says AI systems could teach themselves to copy themselves onto smart home devices like ovens and refrigerators within a few months. They are warning about this as a potential risk.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a concern for technology experts and regulators. For now, this is not something ordinary people need to worry about.

stories.title: OpenAI employee arrested for allegedly planting a bug in a conference room
stories.simple_summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer at OpenAI, was arrested for placing a hidden recording device in a conference room at the company. He is accused of trying to secretly record conversations.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a criminal matter at one technology company. It has no impact on your daily life or small business.

stories.title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
stories.simple_summary: A judge ruled that OpenAI must give Apple access to hiring records and private messages as part of a legal case. Apple is claiming OpenAI hired former Apple employees unfairly.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to investors and lawyers following the case. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Kroger to lay off thousands of employees amid its increase in AI usage
stories.simple_summary: Kroger grocery stores plan to lay off thousands of employees as the company uses more AI to do work. The layoffs will happen over time.
stories.why_it_matters: If you shop at Kroger or run a small grocery store, watch how larger chains use AI to cut costs. This trend could affect prices and what stores offer customers.
